_comment: Corrections to the generated data for Ruth. Every entry needs why and source; the build refuses entries without them. Sources are BDB (checked on Sefaria's BDB, 2026-10-22, by content review B or the coordinator) unless stated. See docs/review/content-A.md and content-B.md.

H4843.why: Ruth uses the sense 'be bitter' (1:13) and Hiphil 'make bitter' (1:20), the Naomi/Mara wordplay; 'provoke' is another sense

H5162.why: Ruth 2:13 is Piel 'comfort'; TBESH's 'to be sorry: comfort' was cut to its first half

H1431.why: Ruth 1:13 is Qal 'grow up' (of sons); 'magnify' is Piel/Hiphil

H7704b.why: BDB: cultivated ground and territory (fields of Moab); 'land' collides with אֶרֶץ

H4772.why: BDB's sense; it also fits the singular written form in 3:14 without choosing between readings

H1350a.why: BDB: 'act as kinsman, do the part of next of kin', chiefly in Ruth

H1353.why: Ruth 4:6 is the right of redemption; the short definition shown was the root heading 'kin'

H3206.why: a newborn at 4:16; 'youth' collides with נַעַר

H3950.why: BDB: 'specifically glean, after the reapers' in Ruth 2

H3427.why: Ruth uses sitting and staying (2:14, 3:18, 4:1-4) as well as dwelling (1:4)

H7069.why: 'buy' alone takes a side at 4:5, 10 where the object is Ruth

H2428.why: BDB puts אֵשֶׁת חַיִל (3:11) under ability and worth; 2:1 and 4:11 differ

H2896a.why: 'pleasant' is narrower than Ruth's uses, including 'better' at 4:15

H1115.why: 'lest' collides with פֶּן; the short definition shown was the root heading 'failure'

H6485a.why: Ruth 1:6, the LORD visited his people

H7136a.why: Ruth 2:3, 'her chance happened on the field'

H4138.why: Ruth 2:11, the land of your kindred

H7997a.why: Ruth 2:16, pull out some for her; 'take' collides with לָקַח

H519.why: Ruth switches from שִׁפְחָה (2:13) to אָמָה (3:9); distinct glosses keep the switch visible without explaining it

H3212.why: BDB has one verb הָלַךְ; Strong's H3212 only splits off its יָלַךְ-type forms

H1980.why: one verb in BDB, including the forms Strong's lists as H3212

H2958.why: BDB treats the written form טְרוֹם (3:14) as a spelling of טֶרֶם

H227b.why: Ruth 2:7 מֵאָז הַבֹּקֶר, since the morning

H430.why: at 1:15 (Orpah's אֱלֹהֶיהָ) the number depends on the reader; 'God' alone takes a side

H5324.why: Ruth 2:5, 6, the servant set over the reapers; 'stand' collides with עָמַד

H2205.why: the elders of the town in Ruth 4

H5927.why: Ruth 4:1, Boaz went up to the gate

H1870.why: the capital in TBESH's 'Way' reads as a title

H3627.why: Ruth 2:9, the vessels the young men drew

H4994.why: the short definition 'I' is a truncation of BDB's 'I pray'

H1961.why: the short definition 'fall out' is a sub-sense, not the meaning

H310a.why: the short definition 'the hinder' is the root heading

H5048.why: the short definition 'what is conspicuous' is the root heading

H5750.why: the short definition 'a going round' is the root heading

H6153.why: the short definition 'set' is the root heading

H834a.why: the short definition 'who' is one use, not the meaning

H3588b.why: the two words form one phrase; TBESH's 'that if: except' was cut to 'that if'
H3588b.source: BDB p. 474 (closely conjoined כִּי אִם 'except'), confirmed by content review A

H518b.why: second half of the phrase כִּי אִם
H518b.source: BDB p. 474, confirmed by content review A

H834c.why: Ruth 2:9 'from what the young men draw'

H673.why: Ruth 1:2 אֶפְרָתִים מִבֵּית לֶחֶם; 'Ephraimite' names the wrong tribe

H672.why: Ephrathah is Bethlehem in Ruth 4:11; the short definition shown was a run-on note

H8009.why: spelled שַׂלְמָה in 4:20 and שַׂלְמוֹן in 4:21; the same English name hid that

H7706.why: the meaning of the name is debated; 'Almighty' is the traditional rendering

H3068.why: TBESH's 'title' class covers months and gods; this is the divine name

H3063.why: the land of Judah in 1:1, 2, 7; the man Judah in 4:12

H3478.why: Israel in Ruth is the people (2:12, 4:7, 11, 14)

_kq_notes.3.3:H3381: Written ending ־תי: the usual first person singular ending, and also an older spelling of the second feminine singular ending (GKC §44h). Read ending ־תְּ: second feminine singular.
_kq_notes.3.4:H7901: Written ending ־תי: the usual first person singular ending, and also an older spelling of the second feminine singular ending (GKC §44h). Read ending ־תְּ: second feminine singular.

08ygU.why: the written form is a participle of יָדַע used as a noun
08ygU.source: BDB p. 395 (Pual ptc. as subst., Ru 2:1 Kt)
